curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8851-1/ (scans; the excavator is pages 1-15, steps 1-19, the bulldozer after)

functions.does: Pump with the red hand pump and push the valve at the left of the cab's back to the side, and the yellow cylinder at the front of the cab raises or lowers the boom, carrying the stick and bucket with it.
functions.source: book: cover diagram (magenta arrow), steps 4-7, 14 and the step 19 inset (first row); the hose from this valve runs to the boom cylinder's base in the model
functions.note: Kinebrick has no pneumatics and the valve is on the frame, so it can't be worked. Dragging the boom p1038 3703 swings the whole arm, but the boom cylinder comes apart: its barrel p263 127 and cap p262 128 are loose parts left on the boom, while its base p264 4701 stays on the cab.

functions.does: The middle valve works the cylinder on top of the boom, which swings the stick in and out at the boom tip.
functions.source: book: cover diagram (green arrow), arm steps 3-4 and 14, the step 19 inset (second row); the hose from this valve runs up the boom to the stick cylinder's base in the model
functions.note: Can't be worked from the valve today. Dragging the stick p1034 3703 swings it with the bucket, but its cylinder doesn't stretch: the rod p1047 337 turns with the stick, the barrel p1049 127 is a loose part left on the boom, and the base p1050 4701 doesn't move.

functions.does: The valve at the right of the cab's back works the cylinder on the stick, which curls the bucket through a pair of links.
functions.source: book: cover diagram (cyan arrow), arm steps 4-6, the step 19 inset (third row); the hose from this valve runs to the bucket cylinder's base in the model
functions.note: Can't be worked from the valve today. Dragging the bucket p1070 4700 swings it alone on the stick-tip axle p1077 3706; the axle p1071 3705 that should join the links to the bucket isn't joined to it, so the links and the cylinder don't follow, and they flop on their own.

functions.does: The hand pump: pushing the red plunger down blows air through the valves, and its spring pushes it back up.
functions.source: book: page 2 (how the pneumatics work), step 10, the step 19 inset
functions.skip: air pressure and the spring aren't modelled; the pump's parts are all loose, on the frame

functions.does: The cab and arm slew round on the turntable above the tracks.
functions.source: book: steps 7-8 and 13 (a turntable, held by a threaded axle and nut); that it slews by hand is inferred
functions.note: The frame is the cab, so the undercarriage is the part to turn. Today it turns, but it drags the sprockets and idlers round with it: six top-run track links (p925, p938, p939, p980, p993, p994, all 3873) are stuck to the cab. The threaded axle p872 8851-73485 and its nuts are loose parts.

functions.does: The tracks roll freely round the 40-tooth sprockets and the 16-tooth idlers; nothing drives them.
functions.note: Partly works today: turning a sprocket rolls the model and spins the idlers on its side, but the track links don't run round; they're stuck to whichever bodies they lie next to.

questions.question: Is the slew meant to turn freely, or is it clamped by the nut?

why: p17 8851-4694c01-f1 is part of the frame
p256 8851-4694c01-f1 is part of the frame
